cases.summary: A write while full is accepted when a read arrives in the same cycle.

result.summary: At cycle 6 the FIFO is full (four entries) and both wr_en and rd_en are asserted. The contract requires accepting only the read, which would drop occupancy to three and clear full, but the RTL's do_write qualifier (line 89) permits a write whenever rd_en is asserted alongside full, so both pointers advance and full remains asserted.

steps.text: Cycles 2–5 perform four writes (c6, e7, d8, e3) filling the DEPTH=4 FIFO; after cycle 5 the reference queue holds four entries and full is true.
Cycle 6 asserts wr_en=1 and rd_en=1 while full=1; the contract row both_full mandates accepting only the read, so the write must be ignored and occupancy should fall to three with full=0.

The RTL evaluates do_write = wr_en && (!full || rd_en) (line 89), which becomes 1 && (!1 || 1) = 1, so the write proceeds alongside the read; both pointers increment, leaving wptr[2]!=rptr[2] and low bits equal, so full stays 1 — mismatching the expected full=0.

likely_cause.text: The write qualifier do_write incorrectly allows a write when the FIFO is full but rd_en is also asserted. The contract requires the write to be ignored in the both_full case; the qualifier should be wr_en && !full (no write when full, regardless of rd_en).

result.next_action: Change line 89 from `wire do_write = wr_en && (!full || rd_en);` to `wire do_write = wr_en && !full;` and re-run the failing simulation tests (random_s1–s4) and the formal full_flag checks.

result.summary: At cycle 3 the FIFO accepted a simultaneous read and write (both_mid). The read should have returned the word 0x83 written at cycle 2, but the design returned 0xd0.
